THE FEATURE: Getting Schooled (X-Men Expansion) lets a character mark advancement boxes between ranks; rules text: 'The player can choose powers that have a prerequisite of the rank that the character is moving up to. For example, if the character is Rank 3 and advances on this chart, the player can pick powers for them that have a Rank 4 or lower prerequisite.' Today the record stores advancement.powerBoxes (see src/domain/character/party.ts, setAdvancementBoxes) and the evaluator already treats a power whose selection reason is 'advancement' as needing only rank+1 (evaluate-character.ts, effectiveRank). But nothing ever sets that reason, and the Builder's power tree keeps next-rank powers locked. Build the missing half:
1. build-options.ts: PowerOption gains `viaAdvancement: boolean`. In powerOptions(), count spare boxes = record.advancement.powerBoxes minus the record's powers that still need a box (reason 'advancement' AND minimum rank above the character's rank). With a spare box, an unselected power whose ONLY unmet requirement is a rank exactly one above the character's becomes state 'available' with viaAdvancement true. Everything else keeps viaAdvancement false.
2. edit-character.ts: togglePower(record, slug, reason: 'purchased' | 'advancement' = 'purchased') records the reason when adding. Removing is unchanged.
3. evaluate-character.ts: new error code 'advancement-powers-over-boxes' on path 'advancement' when the powers that still need a box outnumber advancement.powerBoxes. A power stops needing a box once the character's rank reaches its minimum rank (so a party rank-up, which zeroes the boxes, raises nothing). Plain-words message.
4. sections.tsx, PowerTree only: an option with viaAdvancement toggles with reason 'advancement' and shows a meta label containing the words 'Getting Schooled' (for example 'Uses a Getting Schooled power box'). A selected power whose reason is 'advancement' shows the same label. Do not change anything else in sections.tsx.

It links node_modules, copies the orchestrator's acceptance tests (advancement-powers.acceptance.test.ts, advancement-powers-builder.acceptance.test.tsx) into apps/marvel/src/__accept/, runs the whole vitest suite, tsc, and eslint, prints the tail of any failure, and cleans up after itself. The acceptance tests are the contract; you cannot change them (they are copied in fresh each run). Read them first: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-joe-Agentic-Mini-RPG-Marvel/4ecb59dc-1562-45bb-a475-e78c6af427d7/scratchpad/marvel-tickets/accept/. Every existing test must keep passing. Add your own tests beside the code in the test file you own.

OUTPUT CONTRACT: leave your changes uncommitted in the worktree.
